reading.body:
Nine AI company and AI-focused political committees gave Lisa McClain $26,000 across eleven dated contributions between February 2025 and August 2026, and she voted Yea on every AI bill in the record.

The money is steady rather than concentrated. Microsoft gave twice, $5,000 each time, in April 2025 and March 2026. Amazon gave three times, $2,500 each. Anthropic's committee appears once, in August 2026, at $1,000. Oracle, Palantir, Meta, Google, and Intel each appear once. The contributions span eighteen months with no long gap, which is the pattern of routine fundraising from a member whose committee sits on the receiving end of an industry's standard giving, not of a single decisive transaction.

The four recorded votes are all Yea, on H.R. 7757, H.R. 5764, H.R. 1770, and S. 146, spread from April 2025 to June 2026. The data does not say what any of those bills do, so it cannot support a claim that the votes favored the donors. It also does not say whether McClain sits on a committee with jurisdiction over AI, whether she sponsored anything, or what she said about any of it. Contributions and votes are placed in date order so they can be read together, and that is all the ordering establishes.

What the record does show is that AI money reaches Congress through the same committees that fund everything else, and that the amounts are small. $26,000 over eighteen months is not the scale at which a member's position on compute, permitting, or data center siting would be decided. The binding constraints on AI are buildings and power, and those are settled in state utility commissions, local zoning boards, and interconnection queues, none of which appear here.
